newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. Mideast envoy to visit Egypt for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy to visit Egypt for peace talks.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Egypt on Saturday for talks on the stalled Palestinian-Israeli peace process, Egyptian officials said on Friday.
They said Ross would fly from Israel to the Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh for a meeting with Mubarak, who has often mediated in troubled rounds of peace talks.

Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah, who met with his Egyptian counterpart Amr Moussa on the peace process in Cairo on Friday, is also due to meet Mubarak in Sharm el-Sheikh on Saturday but it was unclear whether he would meet Ross.

Speaking to reporters after almost two hours of talks with Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, Tarawnah said all sides -- especially the United States -- must work hard to push negotiations out of their present rut.

"It is necessary to save the peace process...and we ask the United States, as a sponsor of the peace talks, to put forward initiatives which are balanced and which do not serve the interest of only one side," he said.
Arab countries accuse the United States of being biased towards Israel and Ross has been criticised several times by Palestinians and Arabs alike for what they see as unfair proposals.

Israeli-Palestinian peace talks have been stuck since the Jewish state began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. The Palestinians insist Israel must suspend settlement activity before resuming peace talks.

Ross's visit to Egypt comes as part of U.S. efforts to salvage the peace process. He met Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Friday and was also due to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
On Thursday, Ross said there were difficult problems to solve between the two sides and Palestinian officials said he had not brought any new ideas to restart the talks.
Jordan's King Hussein and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also met on Thursday to discuss the stalled peace process.
